user.title: Add an Aqua Temp heat pump
user.description: Bluetooth devices seen nearby: {total}. Recognized Aqua Temp units: {recognized}. Units already configured are not listed.

device.title: Select your heat pump
device.description: Recognized Aqua Temp units are listed first, followed by other nearby Bluetooth devices (nearest first). If your unit is missing, make sure it is powered on and within range, close the vendor app completely (the unit accepts a single Bluetooth connection), then go back and scan again. As a last resort, some units can be made to advertise by holding the panel button for about 5 seconds until the display shows "bLE".

scan.title: Scanning
scan.description: Looking for nearby Bluetooth devices. This takes about {seconds} seconds…

no_devices.title: No Aqua Temp unit found
no_devices.description:
No unconfigured Bluetooth device was seen nearby.

To make your heat pump visible:

1. Power it on and stay within range — the unit then advertises under a name starting with "BlueNRG".
2. Close the vendor app completely — the unit accepts only one Bluetooth connection.
3. Scan again.

As a last resort, some units can be made to advertise by holding the panel button for about 5 seconds until the display shows "bLE" (on some models this is the WiFi-provisioning gesture).

If no Bluetooth device appears at all, check that Home Assistant has a Bluetooth adapter (Settings → System → Hardware) or an active Bluetooth proxy.

manual.title: Manual address
manual.description:
Enter the Bluetooth address of the unit, e.g. `XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX`. Make sure the vendor app is closed first — the unit accepts a single connection.

Tip: if you do not know the address, make sure the unit is powered on and within range, that the vendor app is closed, and scan again.

test.title: Testing the connection
test.description: Connecting to {address} and probing the unit's data report (connect, request, listen). This can take about a minute.

confirm.title: Name your device

confirm_push.title: Name your device

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the device. Make sure the vendor app is closed (the unit accepts a single Bluetooth connection) and that the unit is in range, then try again.
error.no_response: The device accepted the connection but did not answer. Move closer and try again.
error.crc_error: The device replied, but the response was corrupted. Try again.
error.not_found: Home Assistant can no longer see this device nearby. Make sure the unit is powered on and within range, close the vendor app (the unit accepts a single Bluetooth connection), then scan again.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already configured.
abort.not_supported: This Bluetooth device is not an Aqua Temp heat pump.
abort.no_bluetooth_adapter: Home Assistant has no working Bluetooth adapter or proxy. Plug in a supported adapter (or check the Bluetooth integration), then try again. On container installs, make sure bluez and /var/run/dbus are available.

probe_registers.name: Probe registers
probe_registers.description: Reads the heat pump over BLE and logs every register (raw value, hex, /10) for calibration. The default block triggers the unit's data report and logs every captured block. Close the vendor app first.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Device to probe. Leave empty to probe every configured Aqua Temp unit.

block.name: Block
block.description: Register report to read. "All blocks" triggers the unit's data report; the numbered blocks query one block of the answer burst directly.

power_write_probe.name: Power write probe
power_write_probe.description: Runs the power-write proof probe: sends the vendor's own power-ON frame, verifies the pushed mirror register 2011 follows it, then sends the power-OFF frame and verifies the revert. One WARNING verdict line is logged with the outcome. The unit must be OFF and the vendor app must be closed. Diagnostic measurement, not a control surface.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: Device to probe. Leave empty to probe every configured Aqua Temp unit.

setpoint_write_probe.name: Setpoint write probe
setpoint_write_probe.description: Runs the two-phase setpoint proof probe: phase A writes the register's own current value back (a true no-op — nothing can change) and verifies no neighbor register moved; phase B dips the heat setpoint by 0.5 °C, verifies the pushed mirror register 1046 follows, then reverts it and verifies again. The physical effect: the pool's heat target dips half a degree for about 2 minutes, then returns. One WARNING verdict line is logged with the outcome. Close the vendor app first. Diagnostic measurement, not a control surface.
